steps.what: Teach goal setting, independence and self-advocacy through responsive practice and feedback

tasks.design: Retain personal development teaching and responsive feedback with the teacher. Materials in {DOCS} may support practice, but their separately counted preparation does not shorten the interaction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Learning independence and self-advocacy requires trust, supported choices and adjustment to each student.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing teaching aids can support practice without replacing teacher attention.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing when to offer support and when to allow independent effort.
tasks.human_edge: Building confidence and respecting the student's voice.
tasks.altitude: No change to teaching time or decisions.

reach.task: Reinforce a student's agreed self-advocacy strategy
reach.learn: Consistent prompts and when to reduce support

evidence.claim: Retaining personal development teaching is an E1 design judgement; lesson-preparation studies do not measure this live interaction.

assumptions: Boundary is live teaching and practice, excluding lesson planning and material adaptation.
Student responses are observed during the fully retained interaction; no structured independence score or inferred emotion is assumed.
Zero upkeep because no new software or workflow is introduced.
research_questions: Which prompts help students practise choices without taking those choices away?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Responsive teaching remains fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Encourage exploration and perseverance for later grades

steps.what: Encourage students to explore learning opportunities and persevere with challenging tasks

tasks.design: Retain encouragement, scaffolding and conversations about future learning with the teacher. Existing opportunities in {DOCS} can be discussed without introducing automated motivation or progression decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful encouragement depends on the student's experience, confidence and current challenge.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing information supports the conversation without replacing responsive support.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing challenge with appropriate adjustments and recognising when persistence needs a different approach.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding the learner and making encouragement credible.
tasks.altitude: No change to encouragement time or educational decisions.

reach.task: Discuss accessible learning opportunities for the next grade

evidence.claim: Retaining encouragement and contextual scaffolding is an E1 judgement, with no measured labour saving claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is direct encouragement and exploration, excluding separate transition planning and material preparation.
The teacher elicits interests and observes responses during the fully retained interaction. No automated emotion inference, readiness flag or progression score is assumed.
Zero upkeep because no change is introduced.
unknowns: Student interests and accessible transition options
research_questions: When does a student need a changed task rather than more encouragement?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. All encouragement and scaffolding remain human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Adapt the curriculum to student needs

steps.what: Review curriculum goals and capture students' learning and accessibility needs
Choose instructional techniques, technologies and permitted curriculum adaptations
Modify curriculum materials according to the selected adaptation plan

loop.purpose: Draft a teacher-specified language adaptation of supplied material
loop.input: Source text, selected goals and explicit language and presentation constraints
loop.output: Adapted draft with links to source passages and goal coverage
loop.check: Teacher checks meaning, factual accuracy, retained learning demand and accessibility; unverified alternatives are rejected
loop.stop: One draft and one revision, then manual adaptation
loop.why_not_simpler: Rephrasing while preserving educational meaning requires semantic judgement; layout-only changes use templates

steps.what: Check accessibility and curriculum alignment and approve the exact adapted material for use

tasks.design: Use native layout templates in {DOCS} first and a bounded helper only for teacher-specified text adaptation. The teacher chooses the curriculum and methods, verifies the draft's meaning and accessibility, and approves the exact material before use; support records stay in the {OTHER} pupil record system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rewriting and assembling variants takes time after the teacher decides how to adapt learning.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing lesson editors can draft text at a different level, while teacher review retains instructional control.
tasks.still_hard: Preserving worthwhile learning and meeting an individual student's access needs.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the student and deciding which adaptation supports learning rather than removing it.
tasks.altitude: Less material rewriting; curriculum and support decisions remain with authorised staff.

reach.task: Check that an adaptation preserves the intended curriculum goal
reach.learn: Goal mapping and accessible resource design

evidence.claim: LessonUp rewrites text at another level, summarises and translates; this supports text adaptation capability, not automatic disability-specific curriculum decisions.
Task shares, accessibility checks and savings are E1 estimates, not a transfer of general lesson-planning trial results.

assumptions: Boundary is curriculum adaptation through approved material, excluding live instruction, assessment and support-plan decisions. Common material preparation benefits are assigned once in a roll-up.

The teacher produces goal identifiers, source versions, language constraints, permitted adaptations and accessibility requirements in fully retained s1 and s2. Existing support-plan data are checked, not assumed complete.
The drafting helper receives the minimum task constraints without pupil identity or diagnostic records. Missing or unsuitable source material returns to manual adaptation in s3.
S3 includes draft correction; s4 separately retains final meaning, accessibility and goal checks. No learning-outcome scoring or placement decision is automated.
Test native templates and approved editor features first. National school consultation and access requirements must be checked locally.
unknowns: Approved editor access and data handling
research_questions: Does text drafting save time after checking meaning, learning demand and actual accessibility?

already_counted.description: Draft correction and source meaning checks
Final accessibility, goal alignment and exact-version approval

incremental.description: Maintain adaptation instructions, accessibility examples and approved access

approvals.approved_version: Exact adapted material, source version, goal mapping and accessibility format; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=30+25+30*0.40+15=82; gross=18, upkeep=3, net=15. High assumes reusable source material; low assumes substantial accessibility correction leaves only 3 gross hours offsetting upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe and evaluate student development and health

steps.what: Observe students' performance, behavior, social development and physical health and capture factual notes
Gather current observations and previous records for evaluation
Evaluate student development in context and decide support or safeguarding escalation

tasks.design: Use an access-limited chronological view in the {OTHER} pupil record system to retrieve existing observations. Keep direct observation, first capture, evaluation and escalation decisions with the teacher; the view produces no developmental score or inferred emotion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant factual history can require repeated navigation through records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native pupil record views can reduce retrieval while preserving original notes and context.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing a situational response from a persistent concern and deciding when specialist help is needed.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the student and interpreting observed behaviour in context.
tasks.altitude: Less history retrieval; observation and evaluation remain fully retained.

reach.task: Discuss a contextual observation requiring specialist assessment
reach.learn: Referral boundaries and factual observation standards

evidence.claim: ParnasSys provides pupil records and learning-goal tracking; this supports access to recorded history, not automated health or behavioural evaluation.
Native chronological retrieval and the savings scenario are E1 proposals.

assumptions: Boundary includes observation, current factual notes, relevant history retrieval and evaluation, excluding specialist assessment and duplicate reporting elsewhere.

The teacher produces pupil reference, observation time, activity, factual description and context in fully retained s1. Earlier records were produced by authorised staff during existing work; no new structured health or behaviour score is requested.
S2 retains nine hours for identity, access and relevance checks plus manual retrieval of unindexed notes. No record entry or extraction is made free by the view.
Test native views first. Urgent safeguarding action must not wait for history retrieval; national school consultation and access rules require local confirmation.
research_questions: Can native history views reduce retrieval while preserving context and contradictory observations?

already_counted.description: History relevance, identity and missing-record checks

incremental.description: Maintain view filters and check access boundaries

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=65+15*0.60+20=94; gross=6, upkeep=1, net=5. High assumes repeated navigation; low assumes an existing effective view gives no gross saving while upkeep remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Direct teaching and developmental judgement remain human; material rewriting and history retrieval can take less time.
reach: Check curriculum alignment with instructional coordination
Discuss specialist concerns with school psychology
role.ambitious_version: Use preparation savings for more tailored practice in independence and self-advocacy, within existing support arrangements.
